findings.title: Unsubscribe action crashes when no TopicUser row exists
findings.body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil, e.g. if the logged-in user navigates directly to `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` for a topic they have never visited/been notified about (no TopicUser record has been created for that pair yet). The very next line, `tu.notification_level`, then raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'notification_level' for nil:NilClass`, producing an unhandled 500 error instead of creating/updating the preference (e.g. via the existing `TopicUser.change` helper, which already handles record creation).

findings.title: Unsubscribe mutates notification state via a GET request with no CSRF protection
findings.body: The `unsubscribe` action calls `tu.save!` to change the user's topic notification level, but it is only reachable via GET (`skip_before_filter :check_xhr, only: [:show, :unsubscribe, :feed]` and `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` in config/routes.rb). Rails' CSRF protection does not cover GET requests, so any authenticated user whose browser loads this URL as a side effect (e.g. an `` embedded on another page, a link preview/prefetch by an email client, or a security scanner following links) will have their topic subscription silently changed without consent. State-mutating actions should not be exposed as unprotected GET endpoints.

findings.title: Unsubscribe copy overstates the effect for watching/tracking users
findings.body: When the user's current notification_level is above `regular` (e.g. `watching` or `tracking`), the action only downgrades them to `regular` rather than muting (lines 107-111), but the user-facing text shown immediately after (`topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications` in config/locales/client.en.yml: "You will stop receiving notifications for <title>") and the equivalent copy in the email (`unsubscribe_link` in config/locales/server.en.yml) both unconditionally claim all notifications for the topic will stop. A user who was `watching`/`tracking` and is merely downgraded to `regular` can still receive notifications for direct replies/mentions, contradicting what they were told.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link translation now requires unsubscribe_url, risking MissingInterpolationArgument for other callers
findings.body: The shared `unsubscribe_link` i18n string was changed to require a new `%{unsubscribe_url}` interpolation value. `Email::MessageBuilder#body` and `#html_part` (lib/email/message_builder.rb) call `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` whenever `opts[:add_unsubscribe_link]` is truthy, regardless of whether `unsubscribe_url` was supplied. Only `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` was updated in this PR to pass `unsubscribe_url`; any other existing or future caller of `build_email`/`MessageBuilder` with `add_unsubscribe_link: true` but without `unsubscribe_url` will now raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` and fail to send, where previously the same call worked fine.

findings.title: No automated test coverage for the new unsubscribe feature
findings.body: The PR introduces a security-sensitive controller action (`TopicsController#unsubscribe`), a new model method (`Topic#unsubscribe_url`), and a breaking change to the `unsubscribe_link` translation contract, but adds no controller or model specs covering: a successful unsubscribe for a `regular`-level user, the downgrade behaviour for `watching`/`tracking` users, the slug-mismatch redirect, or the case where no TopicUser row yet exists. The only spec touched here just adds `unsubscribe_url` to an existing MessageBuilder test's options without asserting that the value is actually rendered into the body/html output, or exercising the case where `add_unsubscribe_link` is true but `unsubscribe_url` is missing.

findings.title: Typo in computed property name stopNotificiationsText
findings.body: The computed property is misspelled `stopNotificiationsText` (should be `stopNotificationsText`). It still works because the template at app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs references the same misspelled name, but the typo makes the binding hard to discover via search and is a latent trap: fixing the spelling in only one of the two files later will silently break the unsubscribe page's message.

findings.title: PR description gives no information about the feature
findings.body: The PR description is just "Test 2", with no explanation of the new unsubscribe feature's behavior (including the watching/tracking-to-regular downgrade semantics), rationale, or what was tested, despite the change spanning 18 files including routes, mailer templates, and a new user-facing flow. This makes it hard for reviewers and future maintainers to understand intent or verify completeness.
